questions.q: A diatomic gas $(\gamma=1.4)$ does $100 \mathrm{~J}$ of work in an isobaric expansion. The heat given to the gas is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For Isobaric process $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{w}=\mathrm{P} \Delta \mathrm{v}=\mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}=100 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{u}+\mathrm{w} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{2} \mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}+\mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{f}}{2}+1\right) \mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T} \\ & \left(\frac{5}{2}+1\right) 100=350 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
SECTION - B

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : If dQ and dW represent the heat supplied to the system and the work done on the system respectively. Then according to the first law of thermodynamics dQ=dU-dW.

Reason R : First law of thermodynamics is based on law of conservation of energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below :
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The first law of thermodynamics is stated as dQ=dU-dW. Since dQ is heat supplied to the system and positive thus, dW is work done on the system, i.e., negative work.

We know that the first law of thermodynamics deals with work done, and heat energy supplied or removed from a system. Therefore, it is based on the conservation of energy. The  law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be converted from one form to another.

questions.q: A source supplies heat to a system at the rate of 1000 W. If the system performs work at a rate of 200 W. The rate at which internal energy of the system increases is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, Q=W+U.

Upon differentiation, we get 

dQdt=dWdt+dUdt⇒dUdt=dQdt-dWdt

Given: dQdt=1000 W

dWdt=200 W

Therefore, dUdt=1000 W-200 W=800 W

questions.q: Pressure of an ideal gas, contained in a closed vessel, is increased by $0.4 \%$ when heated by $1^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Its initial temperature must be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Isochoric process
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P} \propto \mathrm{T} \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{0.4}{100}=\frac{1}{T} \\ & T=250 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An ideal gas exists in a state with pressure $P_0$ volume $\mathrm{V}_0$.It is isothermally expanded to 4 times of its initial volume $\left(\mathrm{V}_0\right)$, then isobarically compressed to its original volume. Finally the system is heated isochorically to bring it to its initial state. The amount of heat exchanged in this process is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \omega_1=P_0 v_0 \ln 4 \\ & \omega_2=\frac{P_0}{4}\left(-3 v_0\right)=-\frac{3 P_0 v_0}{4}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \omega_3=0 \\ & \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{T}}=\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\text {cyclic }}+\omega\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{T}}=\omega \quad\left(\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\text {cyclic }}=0\right)$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{P}_0 \mathrm{v}_0\left(\ln 4-\frac{3}{4}\right) \\ & =\mathrm{P}_0 \mathrm{v}_0(2 \ln 2-0.75)\end{aligned}$

Reason (R): Free expansion of an ideal gas is an irreversible and an adiabatic process.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If the container is insulated then temperature is expected to increase in adiabatic compression. So (A) is wrong.
And free expansion is irreversible and adiabatic process. So (R) is correct.

A to B is an adiabatic path and $B$ to $C$ is an isothermal path. The net heat absorbed per unit mole by the system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{AB}}=0 \text { adiabatic } \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{BC}}=\Delta \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{BC}} \\ & =\mathrm{nRT} \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}}\right)=450 \mathrm{R} \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\frac{8 \times 10^{-6}}{6 \times 10^{-6}}\right) \\ & =450 \mathrm{R} \ell \mathrm{n}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)=450 \mathrm{R}(\ln 4-\ell \mathrm{n} 3) \\ & \therefore \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{AB}}+\Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{BC}} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{Q}=450 \mathrm{R}(\ell \mathrm{n} 4-\ell \mathrm{n} 3)\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
7 mole of certain monoatomic ideal gas undergoes a temperature increase of 40 K at constant pressure. The increase in the internal energy of the gas in this process is
(Given R=8.3 J K-1 mol-1)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the given process pressure is constant therefore, it is an isobaric process.

For a quasi-static process the change in internal energy of an ideal gas is independent of the nature of the process and is given by,

ΔU=nCvΔT

=n×3R2×ΔT

[molar heat capacity at constant volume for monatomic gas =3R2]

ΔU=7×32×8.3×40=3486 J

Where, V is the volume, P is the pressure and γ=75 is the ratio of specific heat of diatomic gas

Pmργ=constant  ...2, As V=mρ

⇒PfPi=ρfρiγ

⇒nPiPi=32ρiρi7/5=(32)7/5

∴ n=27=128

questions.q:
The temperature of 3.00 mol of an ideal diatomic gas is increased by 40.0°C without changing the pressure of the gas. The molecules in the gas rotate but do not oscillate. If the ratio of change in internal energy of the gas to the amount of workdone by the gas is x10. Then the value of x (round off to the nearest integer) is _________.

( GivenR=8.31 J mol-1 K-1
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
First, recall the formula of change in internal energy in terms of molar specific heat at constant volume and change in temperature, ∆U=nCVΔT, for diatomic gas, CV=f2R=52R, ⇒∆U=n×52×RΔT

⇒ΔUW=52nRΔTnRΔT=52=2510

So, x=25

questions.q:
The pressure P1 and density d1 of diatomic gas γ=75 changes suddenly to P2>P1 and d2 respectively during an adiabatic process. The temperature of the gas increases and becomes____times of its initial temperature. 

(given d2 d1=32)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For adiabatic process, PVγ= constant

We know, density d=massVolume.

Then, we have Pdγ= constant

Given here, d2 d1=32 and γ=75.

The ratio P1P2=d1 d2γ=13275=1128

The ratio of temperature using ideal gas equation is T1 T2=P1 V1P2 V2=1128×32=14

Thus, T2=4T1.
